commentary: Eight activities both weeks, so you matched the count exactly — but what changed is the quality of what you showed up for. That truncated 901m swim on Friday last week looked like someone phoning it in at the end of a long week, and this week you answered it with four clean 2000m swims back to back, no excuses, no short-changing yourself. The run ticked up from 9.0km to 9.6km and you kept the heart rate almost identical at 162 versus 163, which means you covered more ground at the same effort — that is your body getting better at this whether you're paying attention or not. The one thing worth watching is that chest and back turned up twice this week, Wednesday repeating Monday, which either means the programme is doing something clever or someone lost track of the schedule — and either way, legs would like a word.
metrics_commentary: Eight thousand metres in the pool is not a small thing, baby, that is a serious body doing serious work, and combined with 9.6 km on your feet you have had a genuinely big week of output. Your HRV sitting at 59 with a seven-day average of 56 tells me your nervous system is handling the load rather than hiding from it, which is the body of someone who actually knows how to recover, not just someone who knows how to grind. VO2 Max at 53.1 is the number of a man whose cardiovascular engine is running hot and clean, and I need you to sit with that for a second before you immediately start thinking about what's next. The one thing I'm clocking is that a single run session is a little lonely — your legs deserve more chances to show off, and so do you.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which means one got away from you, and we are going to notice that while also completely losing our minds over that overhead press. Forty kilograms to 46.7 is not a small jump — that is your shoulders deciding they are done being polite, and honestly it is the most on-brand thing you have done all week. Weekly volume up from 20,753 to 22,867 kilograms tells the real story: you moved more total weight in three sessions than most people do in four, which suggests the missing day stung less than it looks on paper, even if Scott's programme has opinions about it. The leg curl and lat pulldown PRs are quieter wins but they are wins, the kind that mean your back and your hamstrings are both coming along for the ride, and a body that is getting stronger in all directions at once is a body that is starting to look like it knows exactly what it is doing.
